findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but the removed embed_category setting stored a category ID string, not a category name, so the join can never match. For every existing production install the category lookup returns empty, category_id resolves to 0 and falls back to the uncategorized category, silently reassigning all embedded-topic routing that previously used embed_category; the advertised data migration never migrates the category.

[BUG] The INSERT interpolates each host string from the old embeddable_hosts site setting directly into raw SQL without quoting or sanitization. Any legacy setting value containing a quote (or the '/'-suffixed and 'http://'-prefixed entries the old setting format permitted) produces invalid SQL or inserts unnormalized values that the new model's before_validation would have stripped, breaking the migration on upgrade for sites whose old setting was not a bare hostname.

[BUG] EmbeddingSerializer declares has_many :embeddable_hosts with embed: :ids, so the show endpoint emits only embeddable_host_ids and never side-loads the embeddable_host records the new store.js plural hydration path (_lookupSubType on each id) needs to resolve. GET /admin/customize/embedding returns an embedding whose ids cannot be hydrated against the payload root, so store.find('embedding') yields a model with no usable embeddable_hosts and the new admin Embedding tab renders an empty table regardless of how many hosts exist in the database.

[BUG] store.find('embedding') is called but no model file for 'embedding' is added in this diff, and the Discourse store resolves models via container lookup of 'model:<type>'. Loading /admin/customize/embedding throws when the store cannot look up the 'embedding' model, making the new admin tab unreachable rather than merely empty.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator contents are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricators. Fabricators load from both files so tests pass, but every future contributor looking for the category fabricator opens embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and vice versa; the next fabricator addition risks compounding the misplacement or duplicate-definition errors.

[ADVISORY] saveChanges calls this.get('embedding').update({}) which PUTs to /admin/customize/embedding, but Admin::EmbeddingController#update only re-renders the serializer and performs no persistence. The save affordance wired to the embedding adapter silently succeeds while changing nothing; users editing embedding-level state (or expecting the PUT to persist anything) get a false confirmation.

[ADVISORY] before_validation mutates self.host with sub! without a nil guard, so EmbeddableHost.new.save (or any record with host nil) raises NoMethodError inside validation instead of a validation error. The admin host-create path where the client can submit a blank host field crashes with a 500 rather than returning render_json_error.

[BUG] The migration inserts raw values from the old embeddable_hosts site setting (which allowed entries like 'http://discourse.org' and 'https://example.com/1234', as the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? accepted and spec/fixtures confirmed) verbatim into the host column, without the scheme/path stripping that EmbeddableHost's before_validation applies. After upgrading, rows like 'http://discourse.org' exist in embeddable_hosts.host, and EmbeddableHost.record_for_host matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` — the bare hostname never equals the scheme-prefixed stored value, so every migrated host silently stops allowing embeds (ensure_embeddable raises InvalidAccess) until an admin re-edits each host.

[BUG] update and destroy look up the host with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and never handle a nil result, so save_host calls `host.host =` on nil and destroy calls `host.destroy` on nil. A PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404; the same applies when params[:embeddable_host] is absent in create/update (`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` on nil → 500).

[BUG] The validation regex requires a dot and 2-5 letter TLD (`[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}`), while the old site-setting path accepted any hostname including single-label names, since the old matcher just compared `h.sub(/^https?\:\/\//, '') == host`. Sites that previously embedded from hostnames like 'localhost' or internal single-label hosts (supported by the old setting matcher, and exercised by the old matcher's equality semantics) can no longer configure them; the admin UI rejects the entry with a validation error with no fallback.

[ADVISORY] The update action is a no-op (it only re-renders the serializer, never reading params), and the only client caller sends `this.get('embedding').update({})` with an empty payload. The PUT /admin/customize/embedding route, the #update action, and the client's saveChanges action are dead code that imply a 'save embedding settings' behavior that does not exist; a future developer wiring settings into this screen will assume the save path works. Since hosts are saved individually via the embeddable_hosts controller, the whole embedding update path could be deleted (route, action, saveChanges).

[ADVISORY] The only specs added for the two new controllers assert subclass-ness; no spec exercises create (params handling, blank category_id defaulting to uncategorized), update, destroy, or the error branch of save_host (render_json_error), and the embedding controller's show/update have no behavioral spec at all. The nil-id 500s above, the blank-category_id→uncategorized defaulting, and the no-op update are all unverified; any regression in the host CRUD contract (the feature's core acceptance path — editing category/host relationships) ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The migration is defined with `change` but performs raw `execute` data manipulation (data migration plus DELETE FROM site_settings) which ActiveRecord cannot reverse, and interpolates setting values directly into SQL strings. Running `db:rollback` past this version raises on the irreversible execute steps; additionally a stored host value containing a quote would produce invalid SQL and abort the upgrade migration.

[ADVISORY] No index is created on embeddable_hosts.host, and EmbeddableHost.record_for_host performs a full-table `lower(host) = ?` query on every embed request (ensure_embeddable) and every TopicEmbed.import. Each embedded-comments page load triggers an unindexed case-insensitive scan of embeddable_hosts; with a large hosts table this adds latency to the embed widget hot path.

[ADVISORY] The delete action's destroyRecord promise has no .catch, unlike save which uses popupAjaxError. A failed host deletion (e.g. 500 from the server) produces an unhandled promise rejection with no user feedback; the row stays in edit mode silently and the admin cannot tell the delete failed.

[BUG] The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines all the category fabricators. Any future reader looking for the category fabricator in category_fabricator.rb (or running a spec load that only requires one file by name) finds the wrong definitions; the diff also makes unrelated destructive edits to the shared category fabricator file that are not traceable to the embedding feature.

[BUG] The PUT /admin/customize/embedding route, EmbeddingController#update, and the client's saveChanges() action (admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7) form a no-op circuit: update ignores its params and re-serializes the same OpenStruct, so saving does nothing. Ships-inert feature: operators get a save endpoint that silently persists nothing; any client or integration that calls update({}) believes changes were saved when they were not. Under-scoped relative to the 'edit embedding' intent — only host CRUD actually works.

[BUG] The migration indexes execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking that any row was returned, so on a site where the embed_category site setting was never set, [0] is nil and the migration crashes with NoMethodError. Migration fails for any production site that never configured embed_category, blocking db:migrate entirely; the cmd_tuples guard used for the embeddable_hosts query two lines later is absent here.

[BUG] The migration interpolates host values from the old embeddable_hosts site setting directly into the INSERT SQL string with no escaping. Any host value containing a quote character in the legacy setting produces invalid SQL and the migration raises; the same string-building pattern is also an unsafe precedent for untrusted setting values.

[ADVISORY] The diff modifies core shared hydration logic (_hydrateEmbedded) and the shared rest adapter basePath to support the embedding feature, expanding scope into infrastructure used by every model. All existing admin models now go through the new type.replace('_','-') and plural-_ids hydration paths; a regression there breaks every embedded-object hydration in the app, not just embedding. The change is traceable but its blast radius is not acknowledged or tested beyond the fruit fixtures.

[ADVISORY] Three explicit method overrides restate exactly what ApplicationSerializer would produce for the declared attributes :id, :host, :category_id. Pure noise: 13 lines that a reader must verify are identical to the default implementation; the next attribute added to the model invites cargo-culted overrides.

[ADVISORY] before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff duplicates the authentication guarantees Admin::AdminController already provides. Two sources of truth for the authorization invariant; a future change to AdminController's filters will silently diverge from these controllers.

[ADVISORY] The saveChanges action calls embedding.update({}) with an empty payload against a server endpoint that performs no persistence, leaving dead client code paired with dead server code. Deletion opportunity: removing saveChanges, the PUT route, and EmbeddingController#update eliminates a whole no-op round trip; keeping them implies a save contract that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import silently drops category selection when record_for_host returns nil (eh.try(:category_id) is nil), with no fallback to any default category as the old embed_category setting provided. If the referer host has no matching EmbeddableHost row (e.g. host added/renamed between retriever check and import, or embed_url differing from referer), the topic is created uncategorized with no signal to the operator; the prior behavior guaranteed a configured category.

[BUG] update loads the host with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes the result to save_host even when it is nil, so host.host= raises NoMethodError. PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id returns a 500 instead of a 404/validation error; the admin UI surfaces an opaque ajax error.

[BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on the result of where(...).first without a nil check, so a missing id raises NoMethodError on nil. DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id for an already-deleted or bogus id returns a 500 instead of success_json or a 4xx; concurrent deletes from two admin tabs hit this.

[BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly, so a POST/PUT without an embeddable_host envelope raises NoMethodError on nil. A malformed API request returns a 500 instead of the 400 the contract should give; the error path is an exception, not render_json_error.

[BUG] record_for_host strips the port from the incoming URL via uri.host but the stored host column is never stripped of its port (before_validation removes only scheme and path, and the validation regex explicitly allows :[0-9]{1,5}), so a host saved as example.com:8080 can never match any referer. An admin adds 'example.com:8080' as allowed host; every embed request from that origin fails host_allowed? and raises InvalidAccess — the configured host silently never works. Conversely the equality lookup matches on bare hostname so a stored bare 'example.com' also authorizes referers on any port, an over-broad match.

[BUG] before_validation mutates self.host with sub! before any presence check, so a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of failing format validation. POST /admin/embeddable_hosts with host omitted (the controller assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] blindly) crashes with a 500 instead of a validation error response.

[BUG] The new fabricator file contains only the category fabricators moved out of category_fabricator.rb and defines no Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while category_fabricator.rb has all of its content removed and specs across this diff call Fabricate(:embeddable_host). Every spec in embed_controller_spec.rb, topic_embed_spec.rb, topic_spec.rb and embeddable_host_spec.rb that calls Fabricate(:embeddable_host) fails with an unknown-fabricator error — the entire new test coverage for this feature is red as written.

[BUG] The advertised PUT /admin/customize/embedding route maps to an update action that only re-renders the fetched embedding and writes nothing. The client's saveChanges (admin-embedding.js.es6 line 7: this.get('embedding').update({})) issues a PUT that silently succeeds while persisting nothing — any future client code assuming this endpoint applies changes gets a green response with no effect.

[ADVISORY] There is no UNIQUE constraint or validation on host, and record_for_host resolves duplicates with .first, so the category that wins for an imported topic is nondeterministic. Two admins can add the same host with different categories; which category receives embedded topics then depends on row order, and the client table shows both rows with no error explaining the conflict. A unique index on lower(host) is the real invariant.

[ADVISORY] embeddable_hosts.host has no index and no foreign key on category_id, while host is now the lookup key for the per-request ensure_embeddable? path and category_id is dereferenced at topic-import time. Every embed comments/retrieve request issues an unindexed full-table scan on embeddable_hosts, and a deleted category leaves orphan rows whose dead category_id blows up PostCreator on the next import from that host.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable replaces an in-memory cached SiteSetting check with a live DB query (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?) on every embed request, with no caching layer added. High-traffic embedded comment widgets now add a DB round-trip per request that previously hit the cached settings object; a slow or saturated DB now degrades the embed endpoint, which is fetched cross-origin on third-party pages.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the embeddable-hosts-present gate entirely, so the condition now depends only on embed_truncate and has_topic_embed?. Behavioral coupling to the host table is removed, which is correct only because has_topic_embed? implies a host existed at import time — but a site that later deletes all its embeddable hosts keeps expandable first posts for all previously imported topics, a state the old setting-based check could not represent.

[ADVISORY] saveChanges sends embedding.update({}) with an empty payload to an endpoint whose update action is a no-op — dead client/server pair with no single purpose. The next developer adding an embedding-level setting will wire it into this update call and discover the server discards the body; the no-op route invites that exact wrong integration.

[ADVISORY] Every attribute (:id, :host, :category_id) is declared and then re-declared as an explicit method returning the identical value — pure duplication with two places to update per attribute. The next attribute addition requires editing both the attributes list and a method block; drift between them produces fields serialized with the wrong source. The explicit methods should be deleted.

[BUG] The new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains only the relocated category fabricators and never defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while category_fabricator.rb had all its definitions removed. Every spec in this diff that calls Fabricate(:embeddable_host) (embed_controller_spec, embeddable_host_spec, topic_embed_spec, topic_spec) raises a Fabrication 'no such fabricator' error, so the entire new test suite cannot run — the acceptance tests for the feature are broken by the file swap.

[BUG] The migration inserts existing embeddable_hosts setting values into the new table via raw string-interpolated SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation that strips 'http(s)://' prefixes and paths. Legacy setting entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' (which the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly accepted, per the deleted site_setting_spec cases) are stored verbatim, so EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's lower(host) = ? comparison against uri.host never matches them — previously working embed sources silently lose embed permission after upgrade; the values are also interpolated unescaped into SQL.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import silently replaces the old embed_category fallback with eh.try(:category_id), producing nil category whenever the source URL host has no EmbeddableHost row. Topics imported for a URL whose host record was deleted after import began (or race window between check and import) are created with no category, changing where embedded content lands without an explicit decision recorded; previously a single site-wide setting guaranteed a deterministic fallback.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the embeddable-hosts condition entirely, so the 'expand first post' behavior is no longer coupled to any configured embed source. Every topic with a topic_embed is expandable even after the admin deletes all embeddable hosts, and the rewritten test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes vacuously (embed_truncate defaults false), so the original intent of the check — gating expansion on a live embed configuration — was silently removed without a compensating behavior.

[ADVISORY] The PUT /customize/embedding endpoint is inert: update re-renders the same OpenStruct without persisting anything, yet the client's saveChanges action calls embedding.update({}) against it. An admin who clicks the settings save on the embedding screen gets a success response for a no-op; the route and controller action shipped in this diff give operators a save affordance that cannot do anything, which is dead surface area that the next change to this screen will have to reason about.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host compares uri.host (which excludes port) against stored host values that the validation regex permits to include a port, so hosts saved with :port can never match. An admin adds 'example.com:8080' (accepted by validates_format_of and the admin UI); embedded comments from http://example.com:8080 are rejected because uri.host strips the port while the stored row keeps it — the host list shows the entry as allowed while the embed check denies it.

[BUG] The migration builds its INSERT statement by raw string interpolation of the stored site setting value: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)" injects the raw host string from site_settings directly into SQL. Any single-quote, backslash, or SQL metacharacter in the legacy embeddable_hosts setting (an admin-entered free-text value, including one tampered with directly in the site_settings table) breaks the migration or executes injected SQL during migrate; this is string-interpolated SQL rather than a parameterized statement.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host compares only URI(host).host against the stored host column, dropping the port, while the validation regex and admin UI explicitly allow stored hosts to carry a :port suffix. A staff member who configures 'example.com:8080' (accepted by the validation regex) gets a record that never matches any referer, because referer hosts never include the port — the configured host is silently inert; conversely a referer on any port (http://example.com:9999) matches the portless stored host, so the port portion of the allowlist is unenforceable in both directions.

[BUG] The rewritten test 'is false if embeddable_host is false/blank' no longer exercises the condition it names: the implementation was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb:869), which never reads embeddable hosts, and the test's before-block is gone, so it passes purely because SiteSetting.embed_truncate defaults to false. The test would pass identically if the old `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? &&` code were restored (in that case the outer scope's blank setting also makes it false), so the suite cannot distinguish old from new behavior — the removal of the embeddable-hosts gate in expandable_first_post? is completely unverified, giving false confidence that the changed branch is covered.

[ADVISORY] The new controller spec asserts only that the class inherits from AdminController and never exercises create/update/destroy or save_host at all. Real controller behavior — params[:embeddable_host][:host] extraction, the blank category_id fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, validation-failure render_json_error, and destroy of a nonexistent id (host.destroy on nil raises NoMethodError) — ships with zero verification; a regression in save_host passes CI. Same pattern in spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:4-8.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator contents are swapped between files: embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains only the :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category fabricators, while category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host). Functionally inert (all fabricator files are loaded) but the next contributor looking for the embeddable_host definition in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, or editing category definitions in category_fabricator.rb, edits the wrong file; the diff even suggests a copy-paste mix-up rather than intent.

[ADVISORY] The basePath change to `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))` is a behavior-bearing change to path routing for all underscored model types, and the diff's only JS tests (test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6) never exercise basePath or admin prefixing. A regression here (e.g. a typo in the replace, or a future type added with dashes) would send embeddable-host CRUD to non-admin URLs and fail auth, and no test in this diff would catch it; store-test.js only covers hydration, not adapter path selection.

[ADVISORY] The updated topic_embed spec covers only the happy path where a matching EmbeddableHost exists; the new `eh.try(:category_id)` nil path (URL whose host has no record, now that embed_category was deleted) has no test. When an embedded URL's host is not registered, PostCreator receives category: nil and topic creation behavior (previously pinned to SiteSetting.embed_category) is undefined/untested; the deletion of embed_category in site_settings.yml means there is no fallback, and no spec asserts what happens.

[ADVISORY] The new plural-hydration tests only assert hydrated record ids that mirror the pretender fixture's color_ids input order, and never cover the `hydrated || []` fallback or an unresolvable id in the list. The data table only contains cases the implementation already handles; if _lookupSubType returns undefined for an id (record not in the payload), obj[pluralize] gets [undefined, ...] and the tests still pass, so the edge case in the changed store.js:196-200 branch ships untested.

[BUG] The `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` guard is dead for a SELECT in PostgreSQL (cmdTuples is only populated for DML), so the INSERT block never runs while the paired `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` always executes. Every existing installation silently loses its configured embeddable host list and embed_category setting with zero rows migrated to embeddable_hosts — the feature appears blank after deploy and the old config is unrecoverable (P0 data loss).

[BUG] `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` in a new shipped migration drops and recreates the table if it already exists, and running the migration again (or on a restored DB where the version row is missing) destroys any hosts admins have configured. Re-running the migration wipes all embeddable_hosts rows; combined with the site_settings DELETE there is no path to recover the host list.

[BUG] Host values from the free-text site_setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), so any value containing a quote or backslash breaks the migration mid-run. A malformed host entry in the old setting aborts the migration after the table was created; on retry with force: true the table is dropped and recreated, and if any hosts had been inserted they are lost.

[BUG] `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError when the SELECT returns no rows (no `embed_category` site_setting row exists, e.g. it was never customized), because `[0]` is nil. Migration crashes on any site that never set embed_category, instead of falling through to the uncategorized fallback that line 13 was written to provide.

[BUG] update and destroy look up the host with where(...).first and pass the possibly-nil result straight into save_host/host.destroy, so an invalid or stale id raises NoMethodError on nil and the API returns a raw 500 where a 404 belongs. An admin with a stale UI (host deleted in another tab) clicks save or delete on that row and gets a 500 error page/popup instead of a 4xx; the row can never be dismissed without a page reload.

[BUG] destroyRecord() has no rejection handler — .then(...) with no .catch — so a failed delete is an unhandled promise rejection with no error surfaced to the user. When the DELETE request fails (network error, 500 from the nil-host path above), the confirm dialog closes, no popup appears, the row remains in the table, and the failure is completely invisible to the admin.

[BUG] saveChanges() fires this.get('embedding').update({}) without awaiting or catching the promise, and the server-side embedding#update action performs no work at all (it just re-renders the serializer). Any caller of saveChanges gets a fire-and-forget PUT whose failure is unhandled, and even on success the endpoint silently drops whatever was intended to be saved — an operation that reports success while doing no work.

[ADVISORY] saveChanges and the server-side embedding#update route are dead/no-op code — the template has no save button bound to saveChanges and the PUT handler persists nothing. Future maintainers wiring a save button to saveChanges will believe embedding-level changes are being persisted when the endpoint is a no-op, producing silent data loss.

[ADVISORY] In the plural hydration branch, `obj[k].map(...)` with `hydrated || []` never falls back to [] (map always returns an array), and ids missing from the identity map become undefined entries in the hydrated list. A payload referencing an unknown embeddable_host id yields an array containing undefined; consumers iterating hosts (e.g. host.category) crash on undefined instead of getting an empty list, and the `|| []` guard gives false confidence that the fallback exists.

[ADVISORY] cancel() on a new record calls sendAction('deleteHost', host) which only removes the record from the local array without calling destroyRecord, so any unsaved host is silently discarded with no server round-trip — inconsistent with the delete path's semantics. Works today because new records were never persisted, but the two removal paths (cancel vs delete) look interchangeable and the next change (e.g. auto-creating hosts) will make cancel silently drop server-side work; also delete passes this.get('host') to deleteHost after destroy resolves, relying on the record still being in the array.

[ADVISORY] The before_validation callbacks use sub! on self.host, which returns nil (raising NoMethodError in the validation chain) when host is nil, and the second sub! strips everything after '/' before format validation so the stored host can never keep a path the UI edit form might show. Saving a host with a nil host attribute (e.g. create with missing params envelope) raises an exception inside validation rather than producing a validation error; on the controller path params[:embeddable_host][:host] nil triggers it, surfacing a 500 where a 4xx validation error belongs.

If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
